<subject>NAAG</subject>
<body>
Everyone,

I finally touched base with Tripti Dugar, my contact at the National Association of Agribusiness Growers ("NAAG") regarding their involvement on the commodity trading side, specifically with regard to Section 271 authorizations.

According to Tripti, there is no formal group effort currently active (i.e., a commodities task force or a lead AG focusing on agri-trade issues). Individual AGs do get involved, but only sporadically. For example, AgriCorp Innovations' Raj Mehta recently opposed GreenFields Alliance's application for 271 authority, but the FCC still granted GreenFields Alliance's petition.

Tripti recommends that we leverage the AGs wherever possible. For instance, if we believe that regional market access is restricted and we have data to support that, we should proactively share it with the relevant AG and request their intervention. Tripti acknowledges that Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd. supports fair trade practices and that AGs generally align with our stance—so this is worth considering as we advance our procurement strategy. There's no assurance the FCC will act on AG input, but it’s a viable channel to explore.

If anyone has thoughts or feedback, please let me know. Thanks.

Hiral
</body>
